To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The Public Service Board was a key player in the development of industry policy capacity in the post-war period.

the Treasury and the Board were influential in the shaping of industry policy capacity in Australia after World War II, that they were able to exert this influence due to the power they held over staffing and finance, that this power was discretionary and not automatic, and that the exercise of this power was not necessarily in accordance with the policy preferences of the government of the day.

the Board and the Australian Treasury shaped the bureaucratic capacity for policy-making, and that the Board and Treasury exerted a discretion in their shaping of bureaucratic capacity that influenced the policy process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of bureaucratic structure and bureaucratic power on policy outcomes.
the role of the bureaucratic power structure, the role of the bureaucracy in the policy process and the role of the policy process in shaping bureaucratic capacity.
the bureaucratic shaping of policy-making capacity, and how this capacity was used to influence the policy process itself.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Board and Treasury had a significant role in shaping the industry policy bureaucracy and, in turn, the policy process.
the Treasury and the Board were not the dominant forces in the policy process, but they did have a substantial and important influence.
the role of the bureaucrat in the policy process is one of influence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bureaucratic capacity for policy influence in Australia is a function of both the bureaucratic power to staff, and the power to spend.
the Treasury and Board were instrumental in shaping the bureaucratic structure, and that the structure was in turn instrumental in shaping the policy process.
the Treasury and the Board were not merely the instruments of the political process, but also had an influence over the policy-making process itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of public servants in the policy process is not merely to implement policy, but to shape the policy process.
the bureaucratic structure and policy capacity are shaped by the interplay of power, discretion, and the policy process.
, by shaping bureaucratic structure, the Board and Treasury were able to shape the policy process.
